regime.note: The September 15–16 minutes show a unanimous 25-basis-point increase to 3.75%–4.00%, and the next FOMC meeting is October 27–28. Low confidence and 64% cash reflect restrictive policy, extended screen leaders, and the analyst book's persistent negative alpha.

thesis: Hold the September 29 event-driven reset through the October 7 settled session. VRTX and NEM remain pre-event positions rather than tape-following trades: Vertex's November 30 povetacicept PDUFA is the core binary catalyst, while Newmont's confirmed October 22 results are 10 trading sessions away. The October 7 whole-universe screen remains crowded: MRNA gained 44.89% over 20 sessions, SHOP 30.95%, CRWD 27.74%, SOXL 26.25%, AMD 23.94%, and MRVL 21.14%; most leaders carry elevated RSI readings or premium/negative earnings multiples. Robinhood fundamentals show VRTX at 29.417343x trailing earnings and NEM at 14.337126x, while the paper book trails SPY by 19.8 points with a -3.57 Sharpe. No new momentum exposure is justified; retain 64% cash, lower confidence to 0.32, and keep weights capped. This is the project's paper-portfolio bridge, not an official plugin investment recommendation.

evidence.point: The September 15–16 FOMC minutes state that all members agreed to raise the target range by 1/4 percentage point to 3.75%–4.00%; the next meeting is October 27–28.
Vertex says FDA assigned a November 30, 2026 PDUFA target date; RAINIER showed a 52.0% UPCR reduction from baseline and a 49.8% reduction versus placebo (P<0.0001).
Newmont says it will release Q3 2026 results after market close on October 22 and hold its call at 5:30 p.m. EDT.
Robinhood's October 8 data shows VRTX at 29.417343x P/E, $126.8623 billion market cap, Q2 revenue $3.3339 billion, Q2 net income $1.0998 billion, and a $576.1111 mean analyst target.
Robinhood's October 8 data shows NEM at 14.337126x P/E, $120.3106 billion market cap, Q2 revenue $6.118 billion, Q2 net income $2.202 billion, and a $139.7629 mean analyst target.
At the October 7 settled close, VRTX was $505.64 and NEM $113.54; VRTX gained 0.66% while NEM fell 2.45% from October 6.

risks: VRTX faces a binary November 30 FDA decision; a delay, rejection, restrictive label, or adverse safety interpretation breaks the thesis.
NEM remains 11.0% below the paper entry; gold-price reversal, cost inflation, or weak Q3 production can overwhelm the valuation case.
A 64% cash balance creates substantial opportunity cost if risk assets continue higher.
The portfolio has produced -19.8 points of all-time alpha with a -3.57 annualized Sharpe; confidence stays low until realized results improve.

reflection.looking_back: The marked book is down 16.0% versus SPY up 3.8%, or -19.8 points of all-time alpha, with a -3.57 annualized 39-session Sharpe. The analyst-memory comparison reports a roughly flat latest book against a 0.5% SPY gain; VRTX is 3.2% below entry and NEM 11.0% below entry.
worked: VRTX and NEM still have company-confirmed future checkpoints, keeping both theses falsifiable rather than dependent on undated momentum.
The 64% cash buffer avoided adding to a screen whose top 20-session leaders gained roughly 21%–45% and were mostly overbought or expensively valued.
missed: The analyst-memory comparison lost another 0.5 point of alpha, so neither event sleeve has earned higher confidence.
NEM fell 2.45% on October 7 while VRTX gained only 0.66%; the Newmont sleeve remains the larger mark-to-entry detractor at -11.0%.
reflection.adjustment: Lower confidence from 0.33 to 0.32, keep VRTX at 20% and NEM at 16%, retain 64% cash, and continue refusing to chase extended semiconductor/software/biotech screen leaders.
